impact:
Reported from real use: the fuel tracker did not reset on a new day.

Cause. `startOfDay` (fuel.ts:22) calls `setHours(0,0,0,0)` and `localDate` (fuel.ts:27) calls `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate`. Both resolve against the *server process's* timezone. Nothing sets TZ in the Dockerfile, cloudbuild.yaml, or docker-compose.yml, so Cloud Run runs UTC. "Local" therefore means UTC, and the user's timezone is never sent, stored, or consulted anywhere in the codebase.

Symptom this produces. For a US Eastern user the server's day rolls at 20:00 local. Anything eaten after 20:00 counts toward tomorrow, and at real midnight nothing resets, because the rollover already happened four hours earlier. Last night's late entries are still on the counter in the morning. The further from UTC, the worse: UTC+13 rolls a day early rather than late.

Blast radius beyond fuel, which is why this is fixed as one model rather than patched in fuel alone:
- `GET /api/fuel/today` totals and `date` (fuel.ts:79, 86), and the day bucketing in fuel history (fuel.ts:138, 151, 154).
- `sessions.ts:24` carries an identical `startOfDay`, so `isToday` is UTC too. A workout logged at 21:00 Eastern creates a session dated tomorrow, and the find-or-create rules (`todaySessionForDay`, `todayFreeformSession`) key on it, so the next morning's session is a second row rather than a resume. Streak and rotation read from the same dates.
- `body_metric.measuredAt` shares the flaw for "last logged Nd ago".

DECIDED APPROACH: the client sends its IANA timezone per request. No stored user timezone preference, and no account-level settings work as a prerequisite.

- The client reads its own zone with `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` and sends it on every request that asks "what is today" — the fuel, sessions, metrics and trends reads, plus the session-creating writes that run through find-or-create.
- An IANA zone name, never a raw UTC offset. An offset is wrong across DST for any historical bucket: scoring a June day against an offset captured in December silently shifts that day's boundary by an hour. `America/New_York` carries the rule; `-05:00` carries one sample of it.
- Day-boundary maths moves off `setHours`/`getDate` and onto zone-aware formatting (`Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `timeZone`, or a date library that takes a zone). Both duplicated `startOfDay` helpers should collapse into one shared module while this is being done — two copies of a timezone rule is how half of it gets fixed.
- Treat the zone as untrusted input: validate it (a bad or absent value falls back to UTC rather than throwing) and decide once, at the boundary, so route handlers receive a resolved zone rather than each parsing a header.
- Historical rows are unaffected and must not be rewritten: stored instants are correct, it is only the bucketing of them that was wrong. Re-bucketing under the real zone will move some past entries between days, which is the fix working, not data loss.

A wrinkle to check while fixing: `performed_at`, `completed_at`, `logged_at` and `measured_at` are all Drizzle `timestamp(...)` without `withTimezone`, so Postgres stores them as `timestamp without time zone`. UTC instants are being written into naive columns, which means the column type cannot disambiguate them either. Worth settling in the same change, since the fix depends on knowing what those instants mean.
resolution:
Fixed as one model rather than a patch in fuel.

`apps/api/src/day.ts` is now the only place a calendar day is decided: `parseTimeZone`, `localDate`, `startOfDay`, `startOfDaysAgo`, `isSameDay`, `isToday`. Both duplicated `startOfDay` helpers (fuel.ts:22, sessions.ts:24) are deleted, so there is no second copy of the rule to fix half of.

The client sends its zone as `?tz=`, appended centrally in the web api client from `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`, read per call so a laptop crossing a timezone reports the new one without a reload. A query parameter rather than a header: a custom header would make every GET a preflighted cross-origin request, and the client deliberately keeps GETs simple to avoid an extra round-trip against a scale-to-zero backend. `resolveTimeZone` middleware resolves it once for `/api/*`, so handlers read `c.get("timeZone")` and never parse it themselves. Anything unrecognized falls back to UTC, which is exactly the previous behaviour.

Worth recording: the tests caught that `Intl.DateTimeFormat` ACCEPTS offset strings like `-05:00` as a timeZone. Validation had to reject offset forms deliberately — an IANA name always starts with a letter, an offset never does — or `?tz=-05:00` would have passed and silently broken DST bucketing, which is the precise failure the IANA-per-request decision exists to prevent.

Timestamps: all nine tracker datetime columns are now `timestamptz`. Migration `0013_timestamps_to_timestamptz.sql` is hand-written `--custom` rather than generated, because drizzle-kit emits `SET DATA TYPE` with no `USING` clause, which reinterprets each naive value in the database session's own TimeZone setting — the same implicit dependency this fix removes. The explicit `USING col AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'` means the conversion says the same thing on any server. `0014` is the generated no-op that syncs drizzle's snapshot so the next `db:generate` doesn't re-emit the change. Better Auth's tables in auth.ts are untouched: 3afya reads them and never migrates them. Verified instants are preserved byte-for-byte across the conversion.

Verified against the running API with the reported scenario. A 21:30 New York dinner (01:30 UTC the next day): under UTC it sits on today's counter showing 40 g, which is the bug as reported; under America/New_York today's counter reads 0 and history buckets it to Sep 11. `/api/fuel/history` buckets it correctly in both zones. `/api/sessions/freeform` find-or-create keys on the local day, so under Pacific/Kiritimati (UTC+14, already the next day) it correctly declines to resume yesterday's session instead of returning it. A malformed `?tz=-05:00` falls back to UTC rather than throwing.

11 new tests in `day.test.ts` cover both US DST transition days (the 23-hour and 25-hour days, where a single-pass offset calculation lands an hour out), the date-line case, offset rejection, and idempotence. Full suite 33 passing, typecheck, lint and build clean.

Not done here, deliberately: `body_metric` has no server-side day logic to fix (BodyScreen computes "last logged Nd ago" client-side), and `seed.ts` still uses `setHours` for demo-data generation, which is not user-facing day logic.

Durable rules added so this cannot recur quietly: umbrella CLAUDE.md gained a "Datetimes carry their zone — always" section covering both the Node and Go blueprints, and 3afya's RULES.md gained rule 6.
title: The day boundary is the server's timezone, not yours: fuel does not reset at local midnight
